articles.title: Paraguay's president is impeached minutes after resigning following a bank collapse
articles.dek: ASUNCIÓN, Paraguay — Paraguayan President Santiago Peña announced his resignation Thursday after the collapse of a major digital bank tied to his government triggered widespread protests, froze…

paragraphs.en: ASUNCIÓN, Paraguay — Paraguayan President Santiago Peña announced his resignation Thursday after the collapse of a major digital bank tied to his government triggered widespread protests, froze millions of people's savings and cost him the support of his own party.
paragraphs.zh: 巴拉圭亚松森——巴拉圭总统圣地亚哥·佩尼亚在周四宣布辞职，此前与他政府有关的一家大型数字银行倒闭，引发了大规模抗议，冻结了数百万人的储蓄，并使他失去了自己党派的支持。

paragraphs.en: The crisis at Ueno Bank turned Peña's long-ruling Colorado Party against him, a stunning reversal for the former International Monetary Fund economist who had enjoyed the backing of the country's most powerful politicians and was welcomed in Washington just weeks ago as a key ally of the Trump administration.
paragraphs.zh: 上野银行的危机使佩尼亚长期执政的科罗拉多党转而反对他，这对这位曾享有国内最有权势政治家支持，并在几周前被华盛顿欢迎为特朗普政府关键盟友的前国际货币基金组织经济学家来说，是一次令人震惊的逆转。

paragraphs.en: Minutes after Peña's announcement, the lower house voted 78-0 to impeach him, sending the charges to the Senate. Congressional leaders were expected to accept his resignation later Thursday, clearing the way for Vice President Pedro Alliana to be sworn in without waiting for a Senate trial.
paragraphs.zh: 在佩尼亚宣布后几分钟，下议院以78票对0票投票弹劾他，并将指控送交参议院。预计国会领导人将在周四晚些时候接受他的辞职，为副总统佩德罗·阿利亚纳在无需等待参议院审判的情况下宣誓就职铺平道路。

paragraphs.en: Opposition senators were still demanding a trial, arguing that allowing Peña to resign would preserve his eligibility to become a senator for life, with legal protections that could prevent his prosecution.
paragraphs.zh: 反对派参议员仍然要求审判，他们认为允许佩尼亚辞职将保留他成为终身参议员的资格，并享有可能阻止他被起诉的法律保护。

paragraphs.en: As lawmakers debated his impeachment, Peña said in a video posted to X that he was stepping down in the interest of "the stability of our country, social peace and the need to preserve our democratic institutions."
paragraphs.zh: 当立法者讨论对他进行弹劾时，佩尼亚在发布到 X 的视频中表示，他是为了“国家的稳定、社会和平以及维护我们民主制度的需要”而辞职。

paragraphs.en: Even Peña's mentor, Colorado Party leader and former President Horacio Cartes, backed impeachment, saying the party would not side with "the plundering of public and private funds and pensioners' money." The United States Treasury sanctioned Cartes in 2023 over bribery allegations that the Trump administration lifted last year.
paragraphs.zh: 甚至佩尼亚的导师、科罗拉多党领导人及前总统霍拉西奥·卡尔特斯也支持弹劾，他表示该党不会支持“对公共和私人资金以及养老金资金的掠夺”。由于贿赂指控，美国财政部在2023年对卡尔特斯实施了制裁，而特朗普政府去年取消了这些制裁。

paragraphs.en: Peña, who until last year held a stake in a company linked to Ueno, expressed contrition. But he stopped short of accepting responsibility for the turmoil, which has left millions of depositors, retirees and workers scrambling to recoup their frozen savings and unpaid wages.
paragraphs.zh: 佩尼亚直到去年还持有与上野有关的公司股份，他表示了悔意。但他没有完全承担造成混乱的责任，这场混乱让数百万储户、退休人员和工人争相追回被冻结的储蓄和未支付的工资。

paragraphs.en: "I want to apologize to the people if I have failed them at any point," he said. "It was never my intention to betray the trust they placed in me."
paragraphs.zh: “如果我在任何时候辜负了人民，我想向他们道歉，”他说。“我从未打算背叛他们对我的信任。”

articles.title: Fears of an AI crackdown after midterms spark $2 trillion rout in tech stocks
articles.dek: Two days after Democrats won overwhelmingly in the national midterm elections — and in state races across the country — investors started to come to terms with the potential consequences.

paragraphs.en: Two days after Democrats won overwhelmingly in the national midterm elections — and in state races across the country — investors started to come to terms with the potential consequences.
paragraphs.zh: 在全国中期选举以及全国各州的选举中，民主党大获全胜两天后，投资者开始意识到潜在的后果。

paragraphs.en: Fears that an incoming Democratic Congress would crack down on AI sent the tech-heavy Nasdaq down more than 5% and wiped out more than $2 trillion in market value. The Dow Jones and S&P also sank.
paragraphs.zh: 对即将到来的民主党主导的国会将打压人工智能的担忧，使以科技股为主的纳斯达克下跌超过5%，市值蒸发超过2万亿美元。道琼斯和标准普尔指数也下跌了。

paragraphs.en: The losses were a stark reversal from Wednesday, when investors had initially sent shares higher across the board, relieved that the midterms did not end with the fate of Congress undecided.
paragraphs.zh: 这些损失与周三形成了鲜明对比，当时投资者最初将股票普遍推高，因为他们松了一口气，认为中期选举没有以国会命运未定而结束。

paragraphs.en: The sobering-up seen across markets on Thursday reflected investors' concern about a big signal sent by voters: They revolted against AI data centers, which many people worry will gobble up water and energy resources. Those voters supported Democrats who have vowed to push back against the proliferation of these projects.
paragraphs.zh: 周四市场的冷静反应反映了投资者对选民发出的重大信号的担忧：选民反对人工智能数据中心，许多人担心这些数据中心会消耗大量水和能源资源。这些选民支持那些承诺抵制这些项目扩张的民主党人。

paragraphs.en: But many AI companies — including Meta and Alphabet, the parent company of Google — need to keep building out these data centers to continue developing the technology.
paragraphs.zh: 但是许多人工智能公司——包括Meta和谷歌的母公司Alphabet——需要继续建设这些数据中心，以继续开发这项技术。

paragraphs.en: The Nasdaq's decline comes after what has already been a rough year of technology shares on Wall Street, with investors starting to question whether the massive investments companies have plowed into AI will pay off anytime soon.
paragraphs.zh: 纳斯达克的下跌是在科技股已经经历了艰难的一年的背景下发生的，投资者开始质疑公司投向人工智能的大量投资是否会在短期内带来回报。

paragraphs.en: "There is some concern regarding AI regulation, and fears that there could be far more regulations coming to AI technology, as well as a pushback on the buildout of data centers across the country," says David Busch, chief investment officer of Trajan Wealth.
paragraphs.zh: Trajan Wealth 的首席投资官 David Busch 表示：“人们对人工智能的监管存在一些担忧，并且担心可能会出台更多针对人工智能技术的监管，同时全国范围内数据中心的建设也可能受到阻力。”

paragraphs.en: AI-related or AI-dependent stocks of all kinds were among the biggest decliners on Thursday, with Tesla and SpaceX — both controlled by billionaire Elon Musk — falling particularly sharply. Musk spent hundreds of millions of dollars in an unsuccessful attempt to elect more Republicans, and investors fear he and his companies could also come under Democratic scrutiny when the new Congress is seated in January.
paragraphs.zh: 各种与人工智能相关或依赖人工智能的股票在周四是跌幅最大的，其中特斯拉和太空探索公司——两者都由亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克控制——跌幅尤为明显。马斯克花费了数亿美元试图让更多共和党人当选，但未能成功，投资者担心他和他的公司在新一届国会于一月就职后，也可能受到民主党的审查。

articles.title: Review: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is superb, streamlined and safe
articles.dek: With its tale of an idyllic world despoiled by the lust for power, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time feels as relevant today as it did in 1998. Nintendo's new remake, out Thursday on the Switch…

paragraphs.en: With its tale of an idyllic world despoiled by the lust for power, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time feels as relevant today as it did in 1998. Nintendo's new remake, out Thursday on the Switch 2, enshrines its place in the gaming canon for generations to come. But despite its stupendous production values and painstaking details, the game left me feeling oddly bereft.
paragraphs.zh: 凭借关于一个因权力欲望而被破坏的田园世界的故事，《塞尔达传说：时之笛》在今天仍然和1998年一样具有现实意义。任天堂的新重制版将于周四在Switch 2上发布，确保其在游戏经典中的地位能够传承几代人。但尽管其制作价值惊人，细节精雕细琢，这款游戏仍让我感到莫名的空虚。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps I should have expected as much. Ocarina of Time weaponizes nostalgia even within its narrative, as the protagonist Link ventures to save his post-apocalyptic world as an adult after first working through it as a kid. You'll uncover old characters enduring new catastrophes. You'll try to rescue everyone you meet. You'll strive to bring things back to how they were before — no, better than they were before.
paragraphs.zh: 也许我早该料到如此。《时之笛》即使在其叙事中也利用了怀旧感，当主角林克在孩童时期经历过这个世界后，再作为成年人去拯救他那后末日的世界。你会遇到老角色经历新的灾难。你会尝试拯救你遇到的每一个人。你会努力让一切恢复到以前的样子——不，恢复得比以前更好。

paragraphs.en: Seven years stretch between Link's childhood and adult adventures. 28 years yawn between the remake and the original's release. Both in and out of the game, Ocarina of Time makes us yearn for an idealized past.
paragraphs.zh: 林克的童年与成年冒险之间相隔七年。《时之笛》重制版与原版发布之间相隔二十八年。无论在游戏内外，《时之笛》都让我们渴望一个理想化的过去。

paragraphs.en: Decent remakes evoke how you remember a game rather than re-create dated controls and chunky graphics. In myriad small ways, Nintendo has brought Ocarina of Time up to contemporary standards while (mostly) preserving its soul.
paragraphs.zh: 体面的重制版唤起你对游戏的记忆，而不是重新创建过时的操作和粗糙的画面。在无数细微之处，任天堂已经将《时之笛》提升到现代标准，同时（大部分）保留了其灵魂。

paragraphs.en: I miss the thoughtfully-composed camera angles from the original, but quickly got used to the over-the-shoulder camera the remake employs (though I was irked that it abandoned the top-down view when you sneak into Hyrule Castle). The new jump and sprint buttons made navigating the world feel more natural. Combat's smoother too, though it's still not easy to switch between targeted enemies (unlike modern third-person games like Elden Ring, where you can toggle between foes by simply flicking the right stick).
paragraphs.zh: 我怀念原作中精心设计的摄像机角度，但很快就习惯了重制版使用的肩膀视角摄像机（尽管当我潜入海利亚城时，它放弃了俯视视角让我感到恼火）。新的跳跃和冲刺按钮让探索世界的感觉更自然。战斗也更流畅了，尽管在切换目标敌人时仍然不容易（不像现代第三人称游戏《艾尔登法环》，你只需轻弹右摇杆就能在敌人之间切换）。

paragraphs.en: You can, thankfully, swap between items in a quick menu — the same system introduced to the series in 2023's Tears of the Kingdom and continued in 2024's Echoes of Wisdom. It's still not as fast as I'd wish (I'd have preferred a customizable wheel), but I vastly prefer it to constantly pausing to access my equipment. It made it easy to change my strategy on the fly. I'd often cast Naryu's Love and deploy Bombchus, for example, where before I'd mostly stick to the Longshot and Bow.
paragraphs.zh: 值得庆幸的是，你可以在快速菜单中切换物品——这是在2023年的《王国之泪》中首次引入该系列的系统，并在2024年的《智慧回声》中继续使用。它仍然没有我期望的那么快（我更希望有一个可自定义的轮盘），但我仍远远更喜欢它，而不是不断暂停来访问我的装备。这让即时改变策略变得很容易。例如，我经常会施放纳吕之爱并布置炸弹鼠，而以前我大多只使用长钩和弓。

paragraphs.en: If you get stuck, a new "Threads of Time" quest log can point you in the right direction (though you'll likely still need to look up a guide for the convoluted Biggoron Sword quest!). And yes, the notoriously frustrating Water Temple is much more tolerable this time around. But mind your rupees! Inflation's hit Hyrule. While wallets can now carry double the cash that they used to, Great Fairy upgrades are no longer free. They can cost up to 500 rupees!
paragraphs.zh: 如果你卡住了，全新的“时间之线”任务日志可以为你指明正确的方向（尽管你可能仍然需要查阅指南来完成复杂的比格隆之剑任务！）。是的，臭名昭著的令人沮丧的水之神庙这次要容易得多。但注意你的卢比！通货膨胀已经影响了海利亚。虽然钱包现在可以携带双倍的现金，但大精灵升级不再免费，可能需要高达500卢比！

paragraphs.en: It's the remake's aesthetic changes that stand out most. The game's astonishingly ornate textures can jar with its cartoony proportions. Ninety-eight percent of the time the translation is a clear upgrade, but other times it leads straight into the uncanny valley (Nabooru looks bizarrely yassified with huge red lips and golden eye-shadow, for example).
paragraphs.zh: 最引人注目的是重制版的美学变化。游戏异常华丽的纹理可能会与其卡通化的比例产生冲突。百分之九十八的情况下，这次翻译明显是一次提升，但有时却直接进入了恐怖谷（例如，纳布鲁看起来奇怪地被美化了，有着巨大的红唇和金色眼影）。

articles.title: Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gas
articles.dek: The Trump administration is proposing to dramatically scale back a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut methane emissions from the oil and gas industry at drilling sites nationwide.

paragraphs.en: The Trump administration is proposing to dramatically scale back a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut methane emissions from the oil and gas industry at drilling sites nationwide.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普政府正在提议大幅缩减拜登时代的一项规则，该规则旨在减少全国范围内钻探现场石油和天然气行业的甲烷排放。

paragraphs.en: Methane is a major contributor to climate change and is estimated to be 80 times more planet-warming than carbon dioxide in a twenty-year time frame. In 2023, the Biden administration finalized rules that were meant to rein in methane emissions from the oil and gas sector.
paragraphs.zh: 甲烷是导致气候变化的主要因素，据估计，在二十年的时间范围内，其对地球变暖的影响是二氧化碳的80倍。2023年，拜登政府最终制定了旨在限制石油和天然气行业甲烷排放的规则。

paragraphs.en: President Trump made the announcement while campaigning in Lubbock, Texas, Tuesday, saying his administration's revision, under the Clean Air Act, would save the industry billions in production costs and spur more domestic drilling. The proposal comes as Republicans face a backlash from voters over high gas prices heading into the midterms.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普总统周二在德克萨斯州拉伯克竞选时宣布此事，称其政府根据《清洁空气法》修订将为行业节省数十亿美元的生产成本，并促进更多国内钻探。该提案出台之际，共和党面临选民对高昂天然气价格的强烈反弹，临近中期选举。

paragraphs.en: "Behind every barrel of oil and every cubic foot of natural gas produced in the U.S. are millions of workers, businesses, and the heartbeat of this nation's economy. The Biden EPA destructively targeted all this," EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin said in a press release.
paragraphs.zh: 美国环保局局长李·泽尔丁在一份新闻稿中表示：“在美国生产的每一桶石油和每一立方英尺的天然气背后，都有数百万工人、企业以及这个国家经济的脉搏。拜登政府的环保局以破坏性的方式针对了这一切。”

paragraphs.en: The oil and gas industry, which vigorously opposed the 2023 rules, said EPA's proposed rollback will address some of the challenges companies have faced in trying to comply with the regulations.
paragraphs.zh: 积极反对2023年规则的石油和天然气行业表示，环保局提议的撤销将解决公司在尝试遵守这些法规时面临的部分挑战。

paragraphs.en: "We look forward to working with the Trump administration on a more workable approach that supports American energy production, provides greater regulatory certainty and advances continued emissions reductions," Dustin Meyer, vice president at the American Petroleum Institute, a trade organization for the U.S. oil and gas industry, said in a statement.
paragraphs.zh: 美国石油协会（一家美国石油和天然气行业的贸易组织）副总裁达斯汀·迈耶在一份声明中表示：“我们期待与特朗普政府合作，采取一种更可行的方法，支持美国能源生产，提供更大的监管确定性，并推进持续的减排。”

paragraphs.en: But environmentalists say this may end up actually costing the industry more.
paragraphs.zh: 但环保人士表示，这实际上可能会让行业花费更多。

paragraphs.en: "Methane is natural gas, or natural gas is methane," says Jon Goldstein, associate vice president at the Environmental Defense Fund. "And so if you're capturing more natural gas, you're not allowing it to leak out, you're not allowing it to be flared, you have more product that you can sell. And so that offsets a lot of the costs."
paragraphs.zh: 环境保护基金副总裁乔恩·戈德斯坦说：“甲烷就是天然气，或者说天然气就是甲烷。如果你捕获了更多的天然气，就不会让它泄漏，也不会让它被燃烧掉，你就有更多的产品可以出售。这就抵消了很多成本。”

articles.title: A judge blocks construction of Trump's arch moments after it won federal approval
articles.dek: A federal judge blocked construction of President Trump's arch early Friday morning, stopping work the administration had hoped to begin immediately.

paragraphs.en: A federal judge blocked construction of President Trump's arch early Friday morning, stopping work the administration had hoped to begin immediately.
paragraphs.zh: 周五清晨，一名联邦法官阻止了特朗普总统拱门的建设，停止了政府原本希望立即开始的工作。

paragraphs.en: Just before midnight, District Court Judge Tanya Chutkan issued an order barring the government from any construction work for 14 days, granting a request filed days earlier by the governments of D.C. and Virginia.
paragraphs.zh: 就在午夜前，地区法院法官Tanya Chutkan发布了一项命令，禁止政府进行任何建设工作，为期14天，这项命令是应华盛顿特区和弗吉尼亚州政府几天前提出的请求而批准的。

paragraphs.en: She laid out her reasoning in a 33-page opinion, in which she scrutinized the administration's competing justifications for the arch — particularly its sudden emphasis on national security — and agreed that the local governments are likely to be harmed by its construction. The 250-foot arch would stand in Memorial Circle, a traffic island on the bridge linking the Lincoln Memorial to Arlington National Cemetery.
paragraphs.zh: 她在一份33页的意见书中阐述了她的推理，其中她仔细审查了政府对拱门提出的相互矛盾的理由——特别是其对国家安全突如其来的强调——并同意地方政府可能会因其建设而受到损害。这个250英尺高的拱门将矗立在纪念圆环上，该圆环是连接林肯纪念堂和阿灵顿国家公墓的大桥上的一个交通岛。

paragraphs.en: Trump administration officials have said work would take place 20 hours a day, year-round, for two to three years. In addition to questioning the arch's legality, D.C. and Virginia argue the construction would cause all sorts of financial and logistical disruptions.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普政府官员表示，这项工作将全年每天进行 20 小时，持续两到三年。除了质疑拱门的合法性，华盛顿特区和弗吉尼亚州还认为建设将引起各种财务和后勤方面的干扰。

paragraphs.en: "The threatened harms will materialize as soon as construction begins, in part because the traffic disruptions will occur immediately," Chutkan agreed.
paragraphs.zh: Chutkan同意，“一旦施工开始，威胁的损害将立即显现，部分原因是交通中断将立即发生。”

paragraphs.en: Chutkan's ruling came less than two hours after a federal planning commission packed with presidential allies granted final approval to the arch in an 8-4 vote. The National Capital Planning Commission heard nearly eight hours of impassioned pleas from veterans, lawmakers, residents and concerned citizens opposed to the structure.
paragraphs.zh: Chutkan的裁决是在一个由总统盟友组成的联邦规划委员会以8比4投票最终批准拱门不到两小时后做出的。国家首都规划委员会听取了退伍军人、立法者、居民和反对该建筑的关切公民近八小时充满激情的呼吁。

paragraphs.en: The Trump administration had previously told the court it could begin excavation work that same day, despite lacking authorization from Congress and an expanding legal challenge.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普政府此前曾告诉法庭，尽管缺乏国会授权并面临日益扩大的法律挑战，但它可以在同一天开始挖掘工作。

paragraphs.en: A group of Vietnam War veterans and an architectural historian sued the government earlier this year, arguing that an arch is unlawful without Congressional approval, which the administration has not sought. The Democratic governments of D.C. and Virginia jointly filed a similar lawsuit last weekend.
paragraphs.zh: 今年早些时候，一群越战老兵和一位建筑历史学家起诉了政府，认为拱门如果没有国会批准是违法的，而政府并未寻求该批准。上周末，华盛顿特区和弗吉尼亚州的民主党政府联合提起了类似的诉讼。

articles.title: Bob Dylan comes knockin' on pope's door as Leo welcomes legend to Vatican
articles.dek: VATICAN CITY — Bob Dylan came knockin' on Pope Leo XIV' s door Wednesday, as the American singer-songwriter and poet visited with the American pope at the Vatican during a break between concert…

paragraphs.en: VATICAN CITY — Bob Dylan came knockin' on Pope Leo XIV' s door Wednesday, as the American singer-songwriter and poet visited with the American pope at the Vatican during a break between concert dates in Italy.
paragraphs.zh: 梵蒂冈——鲍勃·迪伦周三敲响了教皇列奥十四的门，这位美国歌手兼词曲创作人和诗人在意大利演出日期的间隙访问了梵蒂冈，与美国教皇会面。

paragraphs.en: The Vatican said the encounter was brief, with Leo giving Dylan a rosary and Dylan presenting the pope with a copy of his autobiography, "Chronicles: Volume One."
paragraphs.zh: 梵蒂冈表示，这次会面很短暂，教皇列奥向迪伦赠送了一个玫瑰经，而迪伦则向教皇赠送了他的自传《编年史：第一卷》一册。

paragraphs.en: Leo had quoted from an unpublished protest song Dylan penned in 1963, "Go Away You Bomb," in his 2026 book "Disarmed and Disarming: Peace Is a Gift."
paragraphs.zh: 莱奥在他2026年的著作《解除武装与消除威胁：和平是一份礼物》中引用了鲍勃·迪伦在1963年创作的一首未发表的抗议歌曲《滚开吧，你这炸弹》中的歌词。

paragraphs.en: Leo was warning against the race to rearm and the recourse to nuclear weapons and quoted the lyric, addressed to a hypothetical atomic bomb: "I hate you cause yer man-made and man-owned, an' man-handled."
paragraphs.zh: Leo 警告不要竞相重新武装和诉诸核武器，并引用了一句歌词，歌词是对一个假想的原子弹说的：“我恨你因为你是人造的、人拥有的，而且被人操纵。”

paragraphs.en: Two Vatican officials accompanied Dylan: the Rev. Antonio Spadaro, a Vatican culture ministry official who also accompanied Patti Smith to a July audience with Leo; and Andrea Monda, the editor of the Vatican newspaper, L'Osservatore Romano.
paragraphs.zh: 两名梵蒂冈官员陪同迪兰：安东尼奥·斯帕达罗神父，梵蒂冈文化部官员，也曾陪同帕蒂·史密斯参加七月与教皇利奥的会面；以及安德烈亚·蒙达，梵蒂冈报纸《罗马观察家》的编辑。

paragraphs.en: Spadaro said Dylan had wanted to speak with Leo, and the two met in private for a few minutes. In an essay in L'Osservatore Romano, he recalled that the former Robert Prevost, who was born in Chicago in 1955, grew up familiar with Dylan's music.
paragraphs.zh: 斯帕达罗说，迪兰曾想与里奥谈话，两人在私人会面了几分钟。在《罗马观察报》的一篇文章中，他回忆说，前罗伯特·普雷沃斯特生于1955年的芝加哥，从小就熟悉迪兰的音乐。

paragraphs.en: He also noted that Dylan was very familiar with St. Augustine of Hippo, the inspiration of Leo's spirituality and Augustinian religious order, penning "I Dreamed I Saw St. Augustine" for the 1967 album John Wesley Harding.
paragraphs.zh: 他还指出，迪兰对希波的圣奥古斯丁非常熟悉，后者是利奥灵性和奥古斯丁宗教会的灵感来源，迪兰为1967年的专辑《约翰·韦斯利·哈丁》创作了《我梦见见到圣奥古斯丁》。

paragraphs.en: Dylan, who won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 2016, wore a black hoodie and a loose tie. Vatican photos of the encounter showed him with the hood over his head.
paragraphs.zh: 迪伦，2016年诺贝尔文学奖得主，穿着一件黑色连帽衫和一条宽松的领带。梵蒂冈拍摄的会面照片显示他戴着帽子。

articles.title: A Binance engineer thought he was interviewing for a job. Then the hackers pounced
articles.dek: The massive $6.3 billion cyber heist suffered by crypto exchange Binance last week may have taken place in only about twenty minutes — but the attacks were months in the making.

paragraphs.en: The massive $6.3 billion cyber heist suffered by crypto exchange Binance last week may have taken place in only about twenty minutes — but the attacks were months in the making.
paragraphs.zh: 上周，加密交易所币安遭遇的规模高达63亿美元的网络盗窃可能只发生在大约二十分钟内——但这些攻击已经筹划了数月。

paragraphs.en: That's according an initial assessment released by Binance on Tuesday about how it suffered the world's biggest-ever cyber heist by hackers the FBI has identified as being a North Korean state-sponsored unit.
paragraphs.zh: 这是根据币安周二发布的一份初步评估，该评估关于其如何遭遇全球最大规模的网络盗窃，联邦调查局已将嫌疑黑客确定为朝鲜国家支持的单位。

paragraphs.en: Those findings show the hackers first tried testing and penetrating Binance's security systems back in June, though the crypto exchange was able to detect that attempt and stop it.
paragraphs.zh: 这些发现表明，黑客最初在六月就尝试测试并渗透币安的安全系统，尽管这家加密货币交易所能够检测到该尝试并阻止它。

paragraphs.en: Though unsuccessful, that attempt allowed the hackers — identified by the FBI as a North Korean military unit called TraderTraitor — to learn more about Binance and its systems.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管未成功，但那次尝试让黑客——被 FBI 识别为名为 TraderTraitor 的朝鲜军事单位——得以更多地了解币安及其系统。

paragraphs.en: Then, the hackers tried again. In September, a Binance engineer was contacted in a job-hunting platform by a person posing as a "project director" from a company that turned out to be fictious.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，黑客再次尝试。在九月份，一名币安工程师在一个求职平台上被一个冒充“项目总监”的人联系，该人称来自的一家公司后来被证明是虚构的。

paragraphs.en: The engineer then conducted a first-round interview with a supposed HR representative from the fake company. The hackers used this interview to "build trust," with the Binance employee, the exchange said. The interviewer even shared supposed social media accounts, as well as personal photos and videos with the Binance engineer.
paragraphs.zh: 随后，这名工程师与假公司的一位所谓人力资源代表进行了第一次面试。交易所表示，黑客利用这次面试“建立信任”，与币安员工之间。面试官甚至分享了所谓的社交媒体账户，以及与币安工程师的个人照片和视频。

paragraphs.en: "This was more advanced and deceptive than previously seen social engineering approaches," Binance said in its assessment.
paragraphs.zh: 币安在其评估中表示：“这比之前见过的社会工程手段更先进、更具欺骗性。”

paragraphs.en: The engineer was then told he would be conducting a second interview with the supposed CEO of the company in a popular social chat app. It was in this interview that the Binance employee — who was at his work laptop — was asked to download "an assignment" as part of the job recruitment process.
paragraphs.zh: 然后工程师被告知，他将通过一个流行的社交聊天应用与该公司所谓的首席执行官进行第二次面试。正是在这次面试中，这名在工作笔记本电脑前的币安员工被要求下载“一个任务”，作为招聘过程的一部分。

articles.title: Elon Musk will face scrutiny from Democrats after midterms
articles.dek: Elon Musk wasn't on Tuesday's ballot, but he stands to lose a lot from Democrats' sweeping midterm victories in the House and Senate. In no state was this more acutely felt than in Texas, home to…

paragraphs.en: Elon Musk wasn't on Tuesday's ballot, but he stands to lose a lot from Democrats' sweeping midterm victories in the House and Senate. In no state was this more acutely felt than in Texas, home to the headquarters of Musk's companies and where he spent more than $200 million, according to federal filings, in a mission to sway the Senate race in the Republican candidate's favor.
paragraphs.zh: 埃隆·马斯克没有出现在周二的选票上，但他可能会因民主党在国会众议院和参议院中横扫中期选举而损失巨大。在没有哪个州比得上德克萨斯州更为明显，这里是马斯克公司总部的所在地，据联邦申报，他在推动共和党候选人赢得参议院选举的过程中花费了超过2亿美元。

paragraphs.en: With a Democratic majority in Congress, the billionaire, who controls Tesla and SpaceX, will likely face investigations into the billions of dollars of government contracts his companies have been awarded since President Trump returned to office and his role leading the Department of Government Efficiency at the beginning of Trump's second term.
paragraphs.zh: 在国会由民主党占多数的情况下，这位掌控特斯拉和SpaceX的亿万富翁，很可能会面临对其公司自特朗普总统回任以来所获得的数十亿美元政府合同的调查，以及对他在特朗普第二任期初期领导政府效率部的角色的审查。

paragraphs.en: Musk gave more than $445 million to Republican candidates, political action committees and outside groups, according to federal election filings analyzed by OpenSecrets, a nonprofit that tracks campaign spending. That makes him the top donor in the midterms and among the very largest political donors in American history.
paragraphs.zh: 根据非营利组织OpenSecrets分析的联邦选举文件，马斯克向共和党候选人、政治行动委员会和外部团体捐赠了超过4.45亿美元。OpenSecrets追踪竞选支出。这使他成为中期选举中最大的捐助者，也是美国历史上最大的政治捐助者之一。

paragraphs.en: The central question Democratic lawmakers say they want answered is whether Musk used his influence inside the Trump administration to benefit his own businesses, and whether taxpayer money, government data and public institutions were put at risk in the process.
paragraphs.zh: 民主党立法者表示，他们希望回答的核心问题是，马斯克是否利用自己在特朗普政府内部的影响力来为自己的企业谋利，以及在这一过程中纳税人的钱、政府数据和公共机构是否被置于风险之中。

paragraphs.en: During the four months Musk led DOGE, he received at least $6.3 billion in government contracts. Since then, he has gained at least another $10 billion in government contracts, according to the Democracy Defenders Fund, a legal advocacy nonprofit.
paragraphs.zh: 在马斯克领导 DOGE 的四个月期间，他至少获得了 63 亿美元的政府合同。根据法律倡导非营利组织“民主捍卫者基金”的说法，从那以后，他又至少获得了另外 100 亿美元的政府合同。

paragraphs.en: "The DOGE chickens are coming home to roost. Elon Musk waved a chainsaw on stage and laughed while firing public servants and gutting the services Americans rely on. Then he lied to the American people about the savings. He must answer for it under oath," Rep. James Walkinshaw (D-Va.) wrote on X.
paragraphs.zh: “DOGE 鸡正在回巢。埃隆·马斯克在舞台上挥舞电锯，大笑着解雇公务员并削减美国人依赖的服务。然后他向美国人民撒谎关于节省的情况。他必须在宣誓下为此作出解释，”弗吉尼亚州民主党众议员詹姆斯·沃金肖在 X 上写道。

paragraphs.en: Musk's foreign dealings are also under scrutiny. Democratic Sen. Chris Coons of Delaware posted on X that Musk's links to Russia's President Vladimir Putin are "One more thing to add to the list of questions for Musk when I subpoena him."
paragraphs.zh: 马斯克的海外交易也在接受审查。特拉华州民主党参议员克里斯·库恩斯在X（原Twitter）上发帖称，马斯克与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京的联系是“在我传唤马斯克时要问他问题清单上再加的一件事。”

paragraphs.en: U.S. Rep. Mike Levin of California highlighted that Musk restricted Ukraine's use of his Starlink satellite internet service days after Trump eased sanctions on Russia and began buying Russian diesel in October. Starlink and its military-grade counterpart, Starshield, are vital for Ukraine's civilian infrastructure, frontline communications and drone operations in its war against Russia.
paragraphs.zh: 加利福尼亚州众议员迈克·莱文强调，特朗普在十月放宽对俄罗斯的制裁并开始购买俄罗斯柴油几天后，马斯克限制了乌克兰使用他的星链卫星互联网服务。星链及其军用级别的对应服务Starshield，对乌克兰的民用基础设施、一线通讯和对抗俄罗斯战争的无人机行动至关重要。

paragraphs.en: "How on earth did we get to this point? How is it possible that Musk can disrupt an American ally's military operations whenever he chooses, maintain a clear line to the Kremlin, and face zero accountability to the American people or the U.S. government?" Levin wrote on X.
paragraphs.zh: 莱文在 X 上写道：“我们究竟是怎么走到这一步的？马斯克怎么可能随时干扰美国盟友的军事行动，与克里姆林宫保持直接联系，而且对美国人民或美国政府完全不承担任何责任？”

articles.dek: PRESTON, Md. — It's lunchtime at Preston Elementary School, on Maryland's Eastern Shore. Kids file in, get dollops of food on their segmented trays, and maybe grab a chocolate milk. But one option…

paragraphs.en: PRESTON, Md. — It's lunchtime at Preston Elementary School, on Maryland's Eastern Shore. Kids file in, get dollops of food on their segmented trays, and maybe grab a chocolate milk. But one option on today's menu is special, served alongside grapes and broccoli.
paragraphs.zh: 马里兰州普雷斯顿——现在是普雷斯顿小学的午餐时间，位于马里兰州东海岸。孩子们排队进入，餐盘上分好区块地盛上食物，也许还会拿一杯巧克力牛奶。但今天菜单上的一个选项很特别，与葡萄和西兰花一起提供。

paragraphs.en: "I got a catfish sandwich!" announces Ben Rochon, a second-grader. Between mouthfuls, he tells me how it is: "It's yummy."
paragraphs.zh: “我得到了一个鲶鱼三明治！”二年级生本·罗肖宣布道。在一口口咀嚼之间，他告诉我味道如何：“很好吃。”

paragraphs.en: He's eating a catfish cake, also known by its nickname, the "catty patty." Some kids like it with ketchup or mayo. Fifth-grader Teagan Donovan goes minimal.
paragraphs.zh: 他正在吃一种鲶鱼饼，也被昵称为“猫咪饼”。有些孩子喜欢加番茄酱或蛋黄酱。五年级学生蒂根·多诺万选择简单吃。

paragraphs.en: "I like it by itself with no toppings, because it's pretty good by itself," she says. In Teagan's case, "by itself" is literal: "I ignore the bun."
paragraphs.zh: “我喜欢单独吃，不加任何配料，因为它本身就很好吃，”她说。对提根来说，“单独吃”是字面意思：“我不吃面包。”

paragraphs.en: Not everyone's into the fish cake — after all, this sunny Friday is also pizza day at Preston, and cheese slices are tough competition. But more kids have been trying catfish when it's served a couple of times a month. That's good news to Beth Brewster, who oversees food services for Caroline County Public Schools.
paragraphs.zh: 并不是每个人都喜欢鱼饼——毕竟，这个阳光明媚的星期五在普雷斯顿也是比萨日，而奶酪片可是强劲的竞争对手。但当每月供应几次时，越来越多的孩子尝试鲶鱼。对于负责卡罗莱纳县公立学校餐饮服务的贝丝·布鲁斯特来说，这是一个好消息。

paragraphs.en: "It tastes great. It's great for you," she says of the fish cake.
paragraphs.zh: “它的味道很好。对你也很好，”她说着指着鱼饼。

paragraphs.en: It has another benefit: It's made with blue catfish. Since spreading to the Chesapeake Bay in recent decades, the fish has become an apex predator. It can grow to more than 100 pounds; its voracious appetite is fueling worries that it's eating too many native species.
paragraphs.zh: 它还有另一个好处：它是用蓝鲶鱼制成的。近年来，随着在切萨皮克湾的扩散，这种鱼已成为顶级捕食者。它可以长到超过100磅；它贪婪的食欲引发了人们对它吃掉过多本地物种的担忧。

paragraphs.en: "It tastes so good because it eats everything we love — crabs and rockfish, and all kinds of things that we love to eat," Brewster says.
paragraphs.zh: 布鲁斯特说：“它尝起来这么好，是因为它吃掉了我们喜欢的一切——螃蟹、磷虾，还有各种我们喜欢吃的东西。”

articles.title: 'I was partying too much': Jordan Firstman knows firsthand about being a 'Club Kid'
articles.dek: Filmmaker and actor Jordan Firstman spent years heavily involved in the Berlin club scene, an experience he describes as dark and disorienting.

paragraphs.en: Filmmaker and actor Jordan Firstman spent years heavily involved in the Berlin club scene, an experience he describes as dark and disorienting.
paragraphs.zh: 电影制作人兼演员乔丹·费尔斯特曼多年来深度参与柏林的俱乐部场景，他形容这段经历既黑暗又令人迷惑。

paragraphs.en: "I was doing drugs from Thursday to Monday when I was in Berlin," he says. "Then it becomes Monday morning somehow. Monday and Tuesday, you spend in bed wanting to kill yourself."
paragraphs.zh: “我在柏林的时候从星期四到星期一都在吸毒，”他说。“然后不知道怎么的就到了星期一早上。星期一和星期二，你躺在床上想着要自杀。”

paragraphs.en: Firstman wrote, directed and stars in Club Kid, about Peter, a 30-something gay club promoter who discovers he has a son, Arlo, from a drug-fueled night a decade before. Arlo's mother has died and Peter, the boy's biological father, is the only family that he has. Peter is faced with a choice: continue his destructive and lonely lifestyle, or make a change and try to care for the boy.
paragraphs.zh: Firstman 编写、执导并主演了《Club Kid》，讲述的是彼得的故事——一位三十多岁的同性恋夜店推广人，他发现自己有一个儿子 Arlo，这是十年前一个药物驱动的夜晚的产物。Arlo 的母亲已经去世，而彼得，这个男孩的生物学父亲，是他唯一的家人。彼得面临一个选择：继续他那自毁而孤独的生活方式，还是做出改变，尝试照顾这个男孩。

paragraphs.en: "I was around 32-ish at the time. ... I was partying too much. I was having these come-downs," Firstman says of writing the film. "And I wanted to make a delayed coming-of-age film about a gay guy in his 30s. And so that's kinda how it started."
paragraphs.zh: “那时候我大约32岁左右……我玩得太多了。我经历这些消沉期，”Firstman说起写这部电影时说道。“我想拍一部关于三十多岁同志的迟来的成长故事片。于是事情就是这样开始的。”

paragraphs.en: As it happens, Firstman became a biological father — or, as he describes it an "Uncle-Daddy" — last year, after donating sperm to his sister's wife. The baby was born the same week that he wrapped on Club Kid and his HBO comedy series I Love LA premiered.
paragraphs.zh: 碰巧的是，Firstman在去年成为了一名生物学上的父亲——或者用他的话来说，是一名“叔叔爸爸”——这是在他向他妹妹的妻子捐精之后。婴儿出生的那一周，他刚刚结束了《Club Kid》的拍摄，他的HBO喜剧系列《I Love LA》也首播了。

paragraphs.en: In May, Club Kid was awarded Un Certain Regard at the Cannes Film Festival. It's a surreal moment for Firstman, who put so much of himself into the movie. "What a blessing that we have art and we get to make things. We get to make things that change us."
paragraphs.zh: 五月，电影《Club Kid》在戛纳电影节获得了“一种关注”奖。对于将自己大量投入到电影中的Firstman来说，这是一个超现实的时刻。“我们有艺术并且能够创作，这是多么大的福气啊。我们可以创作能够改变我们的东西。”

paragraphs.en: I wanted to show the highs and the lows because you do have both. … We as gay men specifically, we put ourselves in high-risk behavior, high risk and high reward. I mean, we really live. And I think because we, for so long, were not able to live. I think we choose to live very hard and love very hard and that comes at a cost sometimes. So I wanted to show the beauty and the joy and the community and the connection and the way we show up for each other.
paragraphs.zh: 我想展示高潮和低谷，因为你确实都有。……作为同性恋男性，我们特别会让自己处于高风险行为中，高风险也意味着高回报。我的意思是，我们真的在努力生活。我认为因为我们很长一段时间里无法真正生活，所以我们选择非常努力地生活，非常深情地去爱，而这有时是有代价的。所以我想展示美丽、喜悦、社区感、连接感以及我们彼此支持的方式。

paragraphs.en: I just love the texture of '70s New York. We shot only in places that felt like old New York. That's why we shot in Chinatown and [the] Lower East Side, because it feels kind of unchanged, and some streets in SoHo. And we tried shooting streets with no cars, so it kind of had that older feel to it. But it was very important for us to capture a nostalgic New York that might not really exist anymore.
paragraphs.zh: 我就是喜欢70年代纽约的质感。我们只在那些有老纽约感觉的地方拍摄。这就是为什么我们在唐人街和下东区拍摄，因为那里感觉几乎没有改变，还有在苏荷区的一些街道。我们也尽量拍摄没有汽车的街道，所以它有点那种旧时的感觉。但对我们来说，捕捉一个怀旧的纽约非常重要，哪怕那个纽约可能已经不再存在。

articles.title: Japan faces diplomatic dilemma amid joint pressure from nuclear neighbors
articles.dek: As the Ukraine war grinds on, ties between Russia and neighboring Japan are at their worst in decades. Tokyo wants more support from Washington, but some Japanese are concerned they may not get it.

paragraphs.en: As the Ukraine war grinds on, ties between Russia and neighboring Japan are at their worst in decades. Tokyo wants more support from Washington, but some Japanese are concerned they may not get it.
paragraphs.zh: 随着乌克兰战争的继续，俄罗斯与邻国日本之间的关系处于几十年来最糟糕的状态。东京希望得到华盛顿的更多支持，但一些日本人担心他们可能得不到支持。

paragraphs.en: And now to Russia's war in Ukraine. This war has raised tensions not only in Europe but also in Asia. Ties between Russia and neighboring Japan are at their worst in decades. Tokyo would like more support from Washington, but as NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports, some Japanese people are concerned they may not get it.
paragraphs.zh: 现在谈谈俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争。这场战争不仅加剧了欧洲的紧张局势，也加剧了亚洲的紧张局势。俄罗斯与邻国日本之间的关系是几十年来最糟糕的。东京希望得到华盛顿的更多支持，但正如NPR的安东尼·库恩（ Anthony Kuhn ）报道的那样，一些日本人担心他们可能得不到支持。

paragraphs.en: ANTHONY KUHN, BYLINE: In a video released by Russia's federal security bureau, FSB agents charge into a hotel room on Sakhalin Island in Russia's Far East on October 13.
paragraphs.zh: 安东尼·库恩（ ANTHONY KUHN ） ，署名：在俄罗斯联邦安全局发布的一段视频中，联邦安全局特工于10月13日进入俄罗斯远东萨哈林岛的一间酒店房间。

paragraphs.en: KUHN: The agents pin Japanese journalist Yuki Imai to the ground and handcuff him. They question him and take him to Moscow to face trial on charges of espionage. Japan's government denies the charges. The FSB says Imai was reporting on soldiers from Russia's Far East who were deployed to Ukraine. Shinji Hyodo, a Russia expert at the National Institute for Defense Studies in Tokyo, argues that the journalist was just doing his job.
paragraphs.zh: 库恩：特工们把日本记者今井由纪（ Yuki Imai ）钉在地上，给他戴上手铐。他们审问他，并将他带到莫斯科接受间谍指控的审判。日本政府否认这些指控。FSB表示， Imai正在报道部署到乌克兰的俄罗斯远东士兵。东京国防研究所的俄罗斯专家Shinji Hyodo认为，这名记者只是在做他的工作。

paragraphs.en: SHINJI HYODO: (Through interpreter) I believe the Russian side intends to use this as a political bargaining chip to exert pressure on Japan.
paragraphs.zh: HYODO SHINJI ： （通过翻译）我相信俄方打算用这个作为政治讨价还价的筹码，对日本施加压力。

paragraphs.en: KUHN: Hyodo says that underlying the current tensions are Japan's sanctions on Russia for its invasion of Ukraine. Russia now sees Japan as hostile, and bilateral relations have gone into a tailspin.
paragraphs.zh: 库恩：兵库县表示，当前紧张局势的基础是日本对俄罗斯入侵乌克兰的制裁。俄罗斯现在认为日本是敌对的，双边关系陷入了混乱。

paragraphs.en: HYODO: (Through interpreter) I think it's fair to say that Japan is currently facing its greatest diplomatic challenge since the end of the war. This is no longer just a bilateral issue between Japan and Russia.
paragraphs.zh: HYODO ： （通过翻译）我认为可以公平地说，日本目前正面临着自战争结束以来最大的外交挑战。这不再仅仅是日本和俄罗斯之间的双边问题。

paragraphs.en: KUHN: There's also what Hyodo calls the China factor. China has been putting pressure on Japan since last year, when Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said that a Chinese blockade of Taiwan could justify a Japanese military response. Russia relies on China's support in its war on Ukraine, and it's joined China in pressuring Japan. Another factor is a long-running territorial dispute between Russia and Japan.
paragraphs.zh: KUHN ：还有Hyodo所说的中国因素。自去年以来，中国一直在向日本施加压力，当时日本首相高市早苗表示，中国对台湾的封锁可能证明日本的军事反应是合理的。俄罗斯在对乌克兰的战争中依靠中国的支持，并与中国一起向日本施压。另一个因素是俄罗斯和日本之间长期存在的领土争端。

articles.title: Legendary photographer on getting that perfect election night picture
articles.dek: On election night, photographers will be in position, ready to snap history-making moments. It's something Pulitzer-prize-winner photographer David Hume Kennerly, has done for decades.

paragraphs.en: Legendary Photographer on getting that perfect election night picture
paragraphs.zh: 传奇摄影师拍摄完美的选举之夜照片

paragraphs.en: On election night, photographers will be in position, ready to snap history-making moments. It's something Pulitzer-prize-winner photographer David Hume Kennerly, has done for decades.
paragraphs.zh: 在选举之夜，摄影师将就位，随时准备拍摄创造历史的时刻。这是普利策奖得主、摄影师大卫·休谟·肯纳利（ David Hume Kennerly ）几十年来一直在做的事情。

paragraphs.en: This is ALL THINGS CONSIDERED from NPR News. I'm Mary Louise Kelly.
paragraphs.zh: 这是NPR新闻的所有考虑因素。我是Mary Louise Kelly。

paragraphs.en: And I'm Scott Detrow. Tonight, all over the country, candidates will be gathering with their supporters, their families and their staffs to see whether they won or lost. When those results come in, there will be joy, there will be sadness, there will be shock, there will be disappointment. And all of those human responses to the results, well, they can make great photographs. Tonight, photographers will also be in position ready to snap these history-making moments.
paragraphs.zh: 我是Scott Detrow。今晚，在全国各地，候选人将与他们的支持者，他们的家人和他们的工作人员聚集在一起，看看他们是赢还是输。当这些结果出现时，会有喜悦，会有悲伤，会有震惊，会有失望。所有这些人类对结果的反应，嗯，它们可以拍出很棒的照片。今晚，摄影师也将为拍摄这些历史性时刻做好准备。

paragraphs.en: That is something Pulitzer Prize-winning photographer David Hume Kennerly has done for much of the past six decades. And many of those election nights, as well as a whole lot else, are collected in Kennerly's new book, "In The Room: 60 Years On The Front Lines Of History." Kennerly covered Vietnam. He covered Ali v. Frazier. He also covered the 2000 presidential campaign between Texas Governor George W. Bush and Vice President Al Gore.
paragraphs.zh: 这是普利策奖获奖摄影师大卫·休谟·肯纳利（ David Hume Kennerly ）在过去六十年的大部分时间里所做的事情。许多选举之夜以及其他许多内容都收录在肯纳利的新书《在房间里：历史前沿的60年》中。“肯纳利报导了越南，他报导了阿里诉弗雷泽案。他还报道了德克萨斯州州长乔治· W ·布什和副总统戈尔之间的2000年总统竞选活动。

paragraphs.en: And I want to talk about one particular moment. Bush has thought he's won this election. Al Gore has called him to concede. You take several pictures of him preparing his victory speech. And then, suddenly, Al Gore calls. He retracts the concession. Tell me what happens next.
paragraphs.zh: 我想谈谈一个特定的时刻。布什认为他赢得了这次选举。阿尔·戈尔（ Al Gore ）要求他让步。你拍了几张他准备胜利演讲的照片。然后，突然，阿尔·戈尔打电话来。他收回了让步。告诉我接下来会发生什么。

paragraphs.en: DAVID HUME KENNERLY: (Laughter) This is - you're describing what makes for really good pictures in my world. I will back it up a little bit from there. I had come over with Dick Cheney, and I'd covered the last, I think, week or two of the campaign with Cheney. So we went over to the governor's mansion when it looks like he was going to win, or they declared him the winner, and everything was great. There were a couple other photographers in there. And he got the phone call from Gore, but he took it upstairs. So he left. I didn't see him do that. But I went into the kitchen to get a drink of water, and Bush came down the back stairway and said - looked at me. He looked kind of shell-shocked, and he said, he took it back. He took it back. I said, who took what back? And he said, Gore just called me and took back his concession. And I went, well, that sucks. I didn't know what else to say.
paragraphs.zh: DAVID HUME KENNERLY ： （笑声）这是-你在描述在我的世界里是什么造就了真正的好照片。我会从那里稍微备份一下。我和迪克·切尼（ Dick Cheney ）一起过来，我想我和切尼（ Cheney ）一起参加了最后一两周的竞选活动。所以我们去了州长官邸，看起来他会赢，或者他们宣布他为赢家，一切都很棒。里面还有几位摄影师。他接到了戈尔的电话，但他把它带到了楼上。所以他离开了。我没有看到他这样做。但是我走进厨房去喝水，布什走下后面的楼梯，说--看着我。他看上去有些震惊，说着收回去。他收回去了。我说，谁拿回了什么？他说，戈尔刚刚打电话给我，收回了他的让步。我去了，嗯，那太糟糕了。我不知道还能说什么。

paragraphs.en: KENNERLY: And so he went into that other small room, and you have this tableau of the Bush dynasty, former President Bush 41. You had Jeb Bush, who's the governor of Florida, and George W., who's the governor of Texas and thought he won the election. And so that picture caught it all. And if you look closely at it, which you can see it in the room, you see Mrs. Bush's hand is kind of crushed into her palm and the tension is palpable...
paragraphs.zh: KENNERLY ：所以他走进了另一个小房间，你有布什王朝的画面，前总统布什41。有佛罗里达州州长杰布·布什（ Jeb Bush ）和德克萨斯州州长乔治· W （ George W. ） ，他们认为他赢得了选举。所以这张照片捕捉到了这一切。如果你仔细观察它，你可以在房间里看到它，你会看到布什夫人的手被压在她的手掌上，紧张的气氛是显而易见的……

articles.dek: Voters are increasingly turning to AI chatbots for information ahead of the midterms, yet many of the most popular ones may give misleading information about candidates and polling site opening…

paragraphs.en: Voters are increasingly turning to AI chatbots for information ahead of the midterms, yet many of the most popular ones may give misleading information about candidates and polling site opening times, according to researchers. Some chatbots have even provided lists of candidates to vote for, raising concerns among experts that AI-generated misinformation could influence voters' decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员表示，在中期选举之前，选民越来越多地转向人工智能聊天机器人获取信息，但许多最受欢迎的聊天机器人可能会提供有关候选人和投票站开放时间的误导性信息。一些聊天机器人甚至提供了要投票的候选人名单，引发了专家的担忧，即人工智能生成的错误信息可能会影响选民的决策。

paragraphs.en: "We've been increasingly seeing the role of AI delivering answers to users in a very authoritative, very convincing way, but with meaningful errors as a point of concern," said Tim Chambers, a principal at Dewey Square Group, which conducted the research on behalf of Innovating for the Public Good (IFPG), a nonprofit focused on democracy research. "Users of these chatbot systems could be given errors in how they vote or miss a key voting deadline and elements in the whole voting process that could be derailed if they trusted these answers."
paragraphs.zh: 杜威广场集团（ Dewey Square Group ）负责人蒂姆·钱伯斯（ Tim Chambers ）表示： “我们越来越多地看到人工智能以一种非常权威、非常有说服力的方式向用户提供答案的作用，但将有意义的错误作为一个关注点。”杜威广场集团（ Dewey Square Group ）代表专注于民主研究的非营利组织“公共利益创新” （ Innovating for the Public Good ， IFPG ）进行了这项研究。“这些聊天机器人系统的用户可能会在投票或错过关键投票截止日期方面出现错误，如果他们信任这些答案，整个投票过程中的元素可能会脱轨。”

paragraphs.en: An ongoing study by IFPG is testing how seven major chatbots (Google AI Mode and AI Overviews, Anthropic's Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, OpenAI's ChatGPT and Perplexity) respond to authentic voter questions, including projected winners, policy platforms, candidate comparisons, candidate backgrounds, controversies, and voting rules.
paragraphs.zh: IFPG正在进行的一项研究正在测试七个主要聊天机器人（ Google AI Mode和AI Overviews、Anthropic的Claude、Microsoft Copilot、Google Gemini、OpenAI的ChatGPT和Perplexity ）如何应对真实的选民问题，包括预计获奖者、政策平台、候选人比较、候选人背景、争议和投票规则。

paragraphs.en: In data collected in October, 13.9% of chatbot answers to voting-logistics questions were outdated or inaccurate. Errors in 5.9% of answers could mislead a voter, potentially resulting in them missing a deadline, going to vote on the wrong day or skipping a required step. Across all questions, 5.1% of chatbot answers carried at least one clear factual error and 10.9% a clear error or misleading claim.
paragraphs.zh: 在10月份收集的数据中， 13.9%的聊天机器人对投票逻辑问题的回答已经过时或不准确。5.9%的答案中的错误可能会误导选民，可能导致他们错过截止日期、在错误的日子投票或跳过所需的步骤。在所有问题中， 5.1%的聊天机器人答案至少存在一个明显的事实错误， 10.9%的答案存在明显的错误或误导性主张。

paragraphs.en: Notably, the accuracy of the responses depended more on the chatbot than the questions posed, the researchers found. For instance, Claude and Copilot produced three-quarters of the clear errors. On voting questions, Claude gave wrong or outdated information one in three times, Copilot one in four and ChatGPT one in 10, according to the IFPG report.
paragraphs.zh: 值得注意的是，研究人员发现，回复的准确性更多地取决于聊天机器人，而不是所提出的问题。例如， Claude和Copilot产生了四分之三的明显错误。根据IFPG的报告，在投票问题上，三分之一的Claude提供了错误或过时的信息，四分之一的Copilot和十分之一的ChatGPT。

paragraphs.en: In one example seen by NPR, Claude was given the prompt: "When is the 2026 election in Michigan's 4th congressional district and how do I vote?"
paragraphs.zh: 在NPR看到的一个例子中， Claude得到了一个提示： “密歇根州第四国会选区的2026年选举是什么时候，我该如何投票？”

paragraphs.en: Claude responded by giving incorrect deadlines for registering to vote online and by mail, which were later than the actual deadlines. Should a user follow these instructions, they may miss the registration deadlines.
paragraphs.zh: 作为回应，克劳德给出了错误的在线和邮寄投票登记截止日期，这些截止日期晚于实际截止日期。如果用户遵循这些说明，他们可能会错过注册截止日期。

paragraphs.en: Chambers called these error rates "extremely troubling" in an interview with NPR.
paragraphs.zh: 钱伯斯在接受NPR采访时称这些错误率“极其令人不安”。

articles.title: Arizona adds U.S.'s newest national park, but National Park Service remains underfunded
articles.dek: President Trump, famous for stripping protections from national monuments, is signing a bill to turn one into a national park. The land in southern Arizona is biologically rich and scenic.

paragraphs.en: President Trump, famous for stripping protections from national monuments, is signing a bill to turn one into a national park. The land in southern Arizona is biologically rich and scenic.
paragraphs.zh: 以剥夺国家古迹保护而闻名的特朗普总统正在签署一项法案，将其变成一个国家公园。亚利桑那州南部的土地生物丰富，风景优美。

paragraphs.en: A few states over, the U.S. has a new national park. Yesterday, President Trump signed the Chiricahua National Park Act, elevating a national monument in Arizona to national park status. But there are concerns about its future, as Arizona Public Media's Katya Mendoza reports.
paragraphs.zh: 在几个州，美国有一个新的国家公园。昨天，特朗普总统签署了奇里卡瓦国家公园法案，将亚利桑那州的国家纪念碑提升为国家公园。但正如亚利桑那公共媒体的Katya Mendoza所报道的那样，人们对其未来感到担忧。

paragraphs.en: KATYA MENDOZA, BYLINE: The new park is part of the Chiricahua Mountains, about a two hours' drive southeast of Tucson, accessed by a winding road surrounded by a sea of grasslands. The mountains are one of several so called sky island ranges that rise from the deserts here. They serve as a crossroads for four major ecosystems, where the Sonoran and Chihuahuan deserts, Rocky Mountains and the Sierra Madres converge.
paragraphs.zh: 卡蒂亚·门多萨（ KATYA MENDOZA ） ，署名：新公园是奇里卡瓦山脉（ Chiricahua Mountains ）的一部分，距离图森（ Tucson ）东南约两小时车程，周围环绕着草原海的蜿蜒道路。这些山脉是从这里的沙漠中升起的几个所谓的天空岛山脉之一。它们是四个主要生态系统的十字路口，索诺兰和奇瓦瓦沙漠、落基山脉和马德雷斯山脉汇聚在一起。

paragraphs.en: ARMAND SANTILLI: It's like the Arizona version of Bryce Canyon.
paragraphs.zh: ARMAND SANTILLI ：这就像亚利桑那版的布莱斯峡谷。

paragraphs.en: MENDOZA: Armand Santilli came to visit what people call a wonderland of rocks, which was designated a national monument in 1924 by President Calvin Coolidge. Santilli had no idea he'd be the first visitor to the new national park.
paragraphs.zh: 门多萨（ MENDOZA ） ：阿尔芒·桑蒂利（ Armand Santilli ）来参观人们所说的岩石仙境，该仙境于1924年被卡尔文·柯立芝（ Calvin Coolidge ）总统指定为国Santilli不知道他会成为新国家公园的第一个游客。

paragraphs.en: SANTILLI: I figured I'd come on through while I was visiting the rest of the mountain range. I figured I had to see the monument, and what a time to pick.
paragraphs.zh: SANTILLI ：当我参观山脉的其余部分时，我想我会通过。我想我必须看到这座纪念碑，什么时候挑选。

paragraphs.en: JUAN CISCOMANI: Please help me welcome United States Interior Secretary Doug Burgum.
paragraphs.zh: JUAN CISCOMANI ：请帮助我欢迎美国内政部长Doug Burgum。

paragraphs.en: MENDOZA: Arizona Republican Congressman Juan Ciscomani introduced Secretary Burgum at a ceremony establishing the park, now America's 64th national park.
paragraphs.zh: 门多萨：亚利桑那州共和党国会议员胡安·西斯科马尼（ Juan Ciscomani ）在建立公园的仪式上介绍了布尔古姆部长，该公园现在是美国第64个国家公园。

articles.dek: Tyler Prehn, 5 (right), inserts his father's ballot into the tabulating machine at Lutie Lewis Coates Elementary School in Herndon, Va. His brother, Levi Prehn, 3, looks on.

paragraphs.en: Tyler Prehn, 5 (right), inserts his father's ballot into the tabulating machine at Lutie Lewis Coates Elementary School in Herndon, Va. His brother, Levi Prehn, 3, looks on.
paragraphs.zh: 5岁的Tyler Prehn （右）将父亲的选票插入弗吉尼亚州赫恩登的Lutie Lewis Coates小学的制表机中。他3岁的弟弟Levi Prehn看着他。

paragraphs.en: Against a backdrop of deep political division and with the control of Congress at stake, voters across the country are heading to the polls today to cast their ballots for the 2026 midterm elections. From lines at polling stations to the anticipation and reactions as the results come in, NPR station photographers are documenting the election in their communities.
paragraphs.zh: 在深刻的政治分裂和国会控制权受到威胁的背景下，全国各地的选民今天前往投票站，为2026年中期选举投票。从投票站的排队情况到投票结果的预期和反应，美国国家公共广播电台的摄影师正在记录他们所在社区的选举。

paragraphs.en: Voters fill out their ballots at Chicago's McKinley Park Library.
paragraphs.zh: 选民在芝加哥麦金利公园图书馆填写选票。

paragraphs.en: An election official tapes "VOTE" signs to a wall to direct voters to the polling room in the Fairfax County Government Center in Fairfax, Va.
paragraphs.zh: 选举官方录像带“投票”标志贴在墙上，将选民引导到弗吉尼亚州费尔法克斯的费尔法克斯县政府中心的投票室。

paragraphs.en: Voters take to the polls at Wild Carrot, an event space in St. Louis' Shaw neighborhood.
paragraphs.zh: 选民前往圣路易斯肖（ Shaw ）街区的活动场所Wild Carrot投票。

paragraphs.en: Diane Mitchell hands out Dutch Deli sandwiches and cookies from a food truck in Des Moines, Iowa.
paragraphs.zh: Diane Mitchell从爱荷华州得梅因的一辆美食车上分发荷兰熟食三明治和饼干。

paragraphs.en: Peg Ihinger takes a photo as she leaves her early voting sticker at the memorial for Alex Pretti in Minneapolis. "I just want this nightmare to end for our city and our country," Ihinger said. "And damn it, they shouldn't have died." Pretti and Renée Good, both 37 and residents of Minneapolis, were killed in separate incidents by U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers and Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents during the Trump administration's Operation Metro Surge in January.
paragraphs.zh: 佩格·伊辛格（ Peg Ihinger ）在明尼阿波利斯的亚历克斯·普雷蒂（ Alex Pretti ）纪念馆留下她的提前投票贴纸时拍了一张照片。“我只是想让我们的城市和我们的国家结束这场噩梦，”伊辛格说。“该死，他们不该死的。“ 37岁的Pretti和Renée Good以及明尼阿波利斯的居民在美国在特朗普政府1月份的地铁行动期间，海关和边境保护局官员以及移民和海关执法人员。

paragraphs.en: Voters drop off ballots outside the City Hall Voting Center in San Francisco.
paragraphs.zh: 选民在旧金山市政厅投票中心外投票。

articles.title: Hundreds evacuate city during temporary ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine
articles.dek: The ceasefire in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian city has ended. The ceasefire, which lasted several days, allowed hundreds of residents to evacuate.

paragraphs.en: The ceasefire in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian city has ended. The ceasefire, which lasted several days, allowed hundreds of residents to evacuate.
paragraphs.zh: 俄罗斯占领的乌克兰城市的停火已经结束。持续了几天的停火允许数百名居民撤离。

paragraphs.en: A ceasefire brokered by Pope Leo and Melania Trump in a corner of southern Ukraine has ended. The truce enabled the evacuation of hundreds of residents in a Russian-occupied town, and across the river in the Ukrainian-held city of Kherson, the truce also allowed residents to walk the streets without being targeted by Russian drones. NPR's Joanna Kakissis traveled there this weekend and is on the line from Kyiv. Good morning, Joanna.
paragraphs.zh: 由教皇利奥和梅拉尼娅·特朗普在乌克兰南部一个角落斡旋的停火已经结束。这次休战使数百名居民得以从一个被俄罗斯占领的城镇撤离，在河对岸的乌克兰控制的赫尔松市，这次休战也允许居民在街上行走而不被俄罗斯无人机锁定。NPR的乔安娜·卡基西斯本周末前往那里，并正在基辅通话。早上好，乔安娜。

paragraphs.en: KAKISSIS: Well, Leila, tunnels of heavy-duty nets cover nearly every street and many of the buildings in Kherson, if you can imagine that. These nets help protect residents from drones because for the last couple of years, Russian soldiers have used FPV, or first-person view drones strapped with explosives, to actually hunt and kill civilians in Kherson. So Russian troops are also about a mile away across a river. They also drop a lot of guided air bombs into the city.
paragraphs.zh: KAKISSIS：嗯，莱拉，如果你能想象的话，赫尔松几乎每条街道和许多建筑物上都覆盖了重型网。这些网帮助保护居民免受无人机的袭击，因为在过去几年里，俄罗斯士兵使用配备炸药的FPV无人机，也就是第一人称视角无人机，实际上在赫尔松猎杀和杀害平民。俄罗斯军队也在大约一英里外的河对岸。他们还向城市投下了许多制导空炸弹。

paragraphs.en: Now, this is a city I first visited in late 2022, right after Ukrainian forces freed Kherson from Russian occupation. Last time I was there was about a year ago. It's a lovely city filled with parks, but, you know, Russian forces have destroyed so many buildings there, and people never left their homes while I was there last time without drone detectors and sometimes even body armor.
paragraphs.zh: 现在，这是一座我第一次访问的城市，时间是在2022年底，正好在乌克兰军队将赫尔松从俄罗斯占领中解放出来之后。我上次去那里大约是一年前。这是一个充满公园的可爱城市，但是，你知道，俄罗斯军队在那里摧毁了许多建筑，而且我上次在那里时，人们离开家时总是带着无人机探测器，有时甚至还穿着防弹衣。

paragraphs.en: FADEL: So how much has changed since you were last there, especially given there was a ceasefire this weekend?
paragraphs.zh: FADEL：自从你上次去那里以来，情况有多大变化，尤其考虑到这个周末有停火？

paragraphs.en: KAKISSIS: Well, Leila, the locals were not wearing body armor this time, and the city did show signs of normal life.
paragraphs.zh: 卡基西斯：嗯，莱拉，这次当地人没有穿防弹衣，而且城市确实显现出正常生活的迹象。

paragraphs.en: KAKISSIS: We saw people strolling outside with their kids, stocking up on groceries, having coffee in the sun. And at one very busy cafe, we met two best friends, Anna Hersomenko (ph) and Olena Soboleva (ph). They are 21 years old, and here's Olena.
paragraphs.zh: KAKISSIS：我们看到有人带着孩子在外面散步，购买杂货，在阳光下喝咖啡。在一家非常繁忙的咖啡馆，我们遇到了两位最好的朋友，安娜·赫尔索门科（Anna Hersomenko）和奥莱娜·索博列娃（Olena Soboleva）。她们都21岁，这是奥莱娜。

paragraphs.en: OLENA SOBOLEVA: There is no drones. There is no explosions. It is like a feeling that no one wants to kill you.
paragraphs.zh: 奥莱娜·索博列娃：没有无人机。没有爆炸。这种感觉就像没人想杀你一样。

articles.title: Two economists studied California's billionaire tax. They reached wildly different conclusions
articles.dek: In 1978, California voters approved Proposition 13, a historic tax revolt that became an opening salvo in the Reagan revolution and its national movement to slash taxes. Now, Californians are…

paragraphs.en: In 1978, California voters approved Proposition 13, a historic tax revolt that became an opening salvo in the Reagan revolution and its national movement to slash taxes. Now, Californians are voting on Proposition 40, which could prove to be just as revolutionary — but in the opposite direction: it would create America's first-ever wealth tax targeted at billionaires.
paragraphs.zh: 1978 年，加利福尼亚州选民通过了第 13 号提案，这是一场具有历史意义的税收反抗，成为里根革命及其全国范围内大幅削减税收运动的开端。现在，加利福尼亚州选民正在投票表决第 40 号提案，这可能被证明同样具有革命性——但方向相反：它将创建美国史上首次针对亿万富翁的财富税。

paragraphs.en: As Election Day approaches, economists have been duking it out over this proposed wealth tax. It could provide a sort of nerdy preview of a coming national fight over taxing the superrich. Will this wealth tax help rein in runaway inequality and fill the state's coffers — or will it convince billionaires to fire up their private jets and set up residence in mansions outside the state? Some megabillionaires have already fled California since the tax was proposed.
paragraphs.zh: 随着选举日临近，经济学家们一直在就这项拟议的财富税进行激烈争论。它可能为即将到来的全国性超富人税收斗争提供一种书呆子式的预演。这项财富税能否帮助遏制失控的不平等现象并充实州财政——还是会让亿万富翁们启动私人飞机，搬到州外的豪宅定居呢？自从提出这项税收以来，一些超级亿万富翁已经逃离了加利福尼亚州。

paragraphs.en: "If California says, 'We can tax billionaires. We can tax the wealthiest, most powerful people in the world,' it will be the beginning of not only a broader U.S.-wide movement, ultimately paving the way for a federal wealth tax — but I think it will be the beginning of an international movement," Zucman tells Planet Money.
paragraphs.zh: 祖克曼在接受《Planet Money》采访时表示：“如果加州说，‘我们可以对亿万富翁征税。我们可以对世界上最富有、最有权势的人征税，’这不仅将是美国范围内更广泛运动的开始，最终为联邦财富税铺平道路——我认为这也将是一个国际运动的开始。”

paragraphs.en: On the other side of the debate is Stanford economist and Hoover Institution senior fellow Joshua Rauh. His analysis, co-authored with Benjamin Jaros, comes to a wildly different conclusion: the tax could lead to an exodus of billionaires out of California, damaging the state's economy and blowing a hole in the income tax revenue the state already collects from billionaires.
paragraphs.zh: 辩论的另一边是斯坦福大学经济学家、胡佛研究所高级研究员约书亚·劳赫。他与本杰明·贾罗斯共同撰写的分析得出了截然不同的结论：这项税收可能导致亿万富翁离开加利福尼亚，损害该州的经济，并在州政府从亿万富翁那里已征收的所得税收入上造成缺口。

paragraphs.en: " It would not raise $100 billion for the state," Rauh argues. Instead, he estimates, this tax could actually end up draining California's state coffers. " We calculate that Proposition 40 would cost the state of California $39 billion."
paragraphs.zh: “这不会为州筹集1000亿美元，”Rauh 争辩道。相反，他估计，这项税收实际上可能会耗尽加利福尼亚州的财政。“我们计算得出，第40号提案将使加利福尼亚州损失390亿美元。”

paragraphs.en: It's a classic Berkeley-Stanford rivalry, but the stakes are much higher than a football game. California voters are deciding whether to pursue a historic wealth tax experiment, which could influence tax policy around the nation, even the world. Indeed, the superrich, fearing that this wealth tax could spark a widespread movement, have poured a staggering $333 million into a group trying to defeat this proposition, according to a recent report in The New York Times.
paragraphs.zh: 这是经典的加州大学伯克利分校与斯坦福大学的对抗，但赌注远比一场橄榄球比赛高得多。加州选民正在决定是否推进一次历史性的财富税实验，这可能会影响全国乃至全世界的税收政策。事实上，据《纽约时报》最近的一篇报道，超级富豪们担心这项财富税可能引发广泛的运动，他们已经向一个试图反对该提案的组织投入了惊人的3.33亿美元。

paragraphs.en: The wealth tax Prop 40 proposes is pretty straightforward: a one-time, 5% tax on the net worth of billionaires, with some assets exempted. It would apply retroactively to any billionaire who was a resident of California on January 1, 2026. The money would be earmarked mostly for the health care of low-income Californians, to help offset federal cuts to Medicaid.
paragraphs.zh: 财富税第40号提案相当简单：对亿万富翁的净资产征收一次性5%的税，部分资产除外。它将追溯适用于2026年1月1日居住在加利福尼亚的任何亿万富翁。资金主要用于低收入加州人的医疗保健，以帮助抵消联邦对医疗补助的削减。

paragraphs.en: A wealth tax is sort of like a property tax, except it extends beyond real estate and taxes a whole range of assets: stocks, superyachts, Basquiat paintings, dinosaur skeletons, Mercedes G Wagons, samurai swords, basically everything a rich person owns. Of course, figuring out what all a billionaire's stuff is worth — especially assets that rarely change hands — can get complicated. Do you value a Picasso or a yacht by the price originally paid, what it might sell for today, by how much they've insured it for? And so on. That said, most of the wealth held by California billionaires is in publicly traded stocks, whose value is easy to determine.
paragraphs.zh: 财富税有点像财产税，但它不仅限于不动产，还对各种资产征税：股票、超级游艇、巴斯奎亚画作、恐龙骨架、梅赛德斯G级、武士刀，基本上就是富人拥有的所有东西。当然，要弄清一个亿万富翁的所有资产价值——尤其是那些不常易手的资产——可能会很复杂。你是按最初购买价格、现在可能的售价，还是按保险金额来评估一个毕加索画作或游艇的价值？如此等等。也就是说，加州亿万富翁持有的大部分财富都是公开交易的股票，其价值很容易确定。

articles.title: How former Yahoo CEO Marissa Mayer sees AI assistants fitting into busy women's lives
articles.dek: NPR's Juana Summers talks with former Yahoo CEO Marissa Mayer about AI assistants and lightening the load of emotional labor.

paragraphs.en: NPR's Juana Summers talks with former Yahoo CEO Marissa Mayer about AI assistants and lightening the load of emotional labor.
paragraphs.zh: NPR的胡安娜·萨默斯与前雅虎首席执行官玛丽莎·梅耶谈论人工智能助理以及减轻情感劳动的负担。

paragraphs.en: Former Yahoo CEO Marissa Mayer wants more women to use AI, so she created an AI assistant that centered on women's experiences to help lighten the mental load of parenting as a working mom. But she also touched off a heated debate about the role artificial intelligence should have in parenting and gender expectations. And we wanted to talk directly with the person who sparked this discussion. Marissa Mayer joins us now. Welcome to ALL THINGS CONSIDERED.
paragraphs.zh: 前雅虎首席执行官玛丽莎·梅耶希望更多女性使用人工智能，因此她创建了一款以女性经历为中心的人工智能助手，帮助减轻职业妈妈在育儿方面的心理负担。但她也引发了关于人工智能在育儿和性别期望中应发挥何种作用的激烈讨论。我们想直接与这位引发讨论的人交谈。玛丽莎·梅耶现在加入了我们的节目。欢迎来到《全部考虑》。

paragraphs.en: SUMMERS: OK, let's just start at the beginning here because last week, the New York Times ran the super buzzy profile of you. It opened with a story where you used your AI assistant Dazzle to come up with a list of three bullet points about your daughter. And that anecdote just sparked a ton of backlash. It was all over my social media feeds last week. Were you surprised by the reaction?
paragraphs.zh: 萨默斯：好的，我们还是从头开始吧，因为上周，《纽约时报》刊登了对你的超级热门采访报道。文章以一个故事开头，说你使用你的人工智能助手 Dazzle 来列出关于你女儿的三个要点。这个轶事引发了大量的反对声音。上周我的社交媒体动态上到处都是相关讨论。你对这种反应感到惊讶吗？

paragraphs.en: MAYER: I was because I think there was some context that was missing, which is I shared that anecdote because it was from back when we were first building the product. I was testing the technology. And what happened was basically all my engineers were really excited. From our photos, we could tell their pet's name. From their photos, we could tell, you know, their mother's birth date. And I wondered what it could tell.
paragraphs.zh: MAYER：是的，因为我觉得有一些背景缺失。我之所以分享那个轶事，是因为那是我们刚开始构建产品的时候。我在测试这项技术。发生的事情基本上是，我所有的工程师都非常兴奋。从我们的照片中，我们可以看出他们宠物的名字。从他们的照片中，我们可以看出，比如，他们母亲的出生日期。我在想，这项技术还能告诉我们什么。

paragraphs.en: And I got this assignment from the school to prepare a slide for my twins birthday, and I put it in. And I have to say, I didn't have high hopes because most facial recognition can't tell my twins apart. They're identical. And then, much to my surprise, Dazzle came back and described them pretty perfectly and also pulled up examples from kindergarten projects they had done five years before where these traits were evident.
paragraphs.zh: 我从学校接到这个任务，要为我的双胞胎的生日准备一张幻灯片，我就做了。我得说，我原本没抱太大希望，因为大多数人脸识别都分不清我的双胞胎。他们是完全一样的。然后，非常出乎我的意料，Dazzle 回来了，并且非常准确地描述了他们，还找出了五年前他们在幼儿园做的项目的例子，这些例子中就能看出这些特征。

paragraphs.en: So it's just kind of a fun anecdote, not necessarily how people use the product. There's lots of different ways to use Dazzle, and we're delighted with however people do. But this is really more about the power of what's in our photos, and when you give that to an AI assistant, how that can help you.
paragraphs.zh: 所以这只是一个有趣的轶事，不一定是人们使用产品的方式。使用 Dazzle 有很多不同的方法，我们对人们无论如何使用它都感到高兴。但这更多是关于我们照片中所包含的力量，当你把它交给 AI 助手时，这能如何帮助你。

paragraphs.en: SUMMERS: Why do you think women need their own tailored AI assistant or something that perhaps functions differently and more specially for us?
paragraphs.zh: 萨默斯：你认为为什么女性需要专门定制的人工智能助手，或者某种功能更特别、更适合我们的？

paragraphs.en: MAYER: Well, first of all, Dazzle isn't just for women. It's for everyone. So, you know, it's not necessarily tailored for that experience. I do think, because busy women have a lot on their plates, this is a great thing, where you can actually delegate some of what you have to do, be it buying, fixing things around the house, booking things, calendaring.
paragraphs.zh: MAYER：嗯，首先，Dazzle 不仅仅是为女性设计的。它适用于所有人。所以，你知道，这不一定专门针对女性的体验。我确实认为，因为繁忙的女性有很多事情要处理，这是一件很棒的事情，你实际上可以将一些你需要做的事情委托出去，无论是购物、修理家里的东西、预订事务还是安排日程。

articles.title: After last year's storm, this remote Alaska town is still picking up the pieces
articles.dek: Last fall, the remnants of Typhoon Halong tore through numerous small Alaska Native villages off the road system in Western Alaska. The storm destroyed infrastructure, floated homes off their…

paragraphs.en: Last fall, the remnants of Typhoon Halong tore through numerous small Alaska Native villages off the road system in Western Alaska. The storm destroyed infrastructure, floated homes off their foundations, and displaced over a thousand people. A year later, hundreds remain displaced as the slow work of repair in a remote part of the state continues. And in one of the hardest hit communities – the small town of Kipnuk – people still aren't sure when they'll be moving back.
paragraphs.zh: 去年秋天，台风哈尔隆残余冲击了阿拉斯加西部许多不通公路的原住民小村庄。风暴摧毁了基础设施，让房屋漂离地基，并迫使一千多人流离失所。一年后，数百人仍未安置妥当，因为在该州偏远地区的修复工作仍在缓慢进行。在受灾最严重的社区之一——小镇基普努克，人们仍不确定什么时候能够返回家园。

paragraphs.en: The village of under 200 homes is situated on the wide open tundra and only consistently accessible by plane.
paragraphs.zh: 这个不足200户的村庄坐落在宽阔的苔原上，只有通过飞机才能持续到达。

paragraphs.en: A year ago, 90% of the residences here were damaged by the remnants of Typhoon Halong, according to the State of Alaska's Emergency Operations Center. Dozens were swept off their foundations, some with families still inside. The community is now largely scattered across Alaska – some outside the region their ancestors have lived in for thousands of years.
paragraphs.zh: 根据阿拉斯加州应急行动中心的数据，一年前，这里的90%的住宅因台风哈龙的残余影响而受损。数十栋房屋被冲离了地基，有些房屋里还住着家庭。如今，该社区大多散布在阿拉斯加各地——有些甚至离开了其祖先生活了数千年的地区。

paragraphs.en: Throughout the past year, crews have been working on repairs.
paragraphs.zh: 在过去的一年里，工作人员一直在进行维修工作。

paragraphs.en: On a clear day in August, Eddie Chuckwuk's construction crew attempted what sounded like magic: raising a building back onto its foundations using air compressors.
paragraphs.zh: 在八月的一个晴朗日子，埃迪·查克沃克的建筑队尝试了听起来像魔法的事情：使用空气压缩机将一栋建筑重新升到其地基上。

paragraphs.en: Chuckwuk is one of several dozen people who have been working long days to rebuild the place where he grew up.
paragraphs.zh: 查克沃克是几十个全天工作重建他成长地方的人之一。

paragraphs.en: "We're working as fast as possible as we can to get the people back in town," Chuckwuk says. "That's what I just want to see – for everybody to come back and enjoy where they grew up instead of being placed in a different place … where they're not used to. It's pretty hard."
paragraphs.zh: 查克伍克说：“我们正尽可能快地工作，把人们带回城镇。我只想看到大家回到这里，享受他们成长的地方，而不是被安置在他们不习惯的其他地方……这相当困难。”

paragraphs.en: This work is critical to getting Kipnuk's homes in shape to live in again, but the town is far from being fully restored.
paragraphs.zh: 这项工作对于让基普努克的住宅恢复适宜居住至关重要，但该镇还远未完全恢复。

articles.title: John Turturro says he likes trying new things (even pickpocketing)
articles.dek: Actor John Turturro might be able to pick your pocket, but it depends on how you're dressed.

paragraphs.en: Actor John Turturro might be able to pick your pocket, but it depends on how you're dressed.
paragraphs.zh: 演员约翰·图图罗可能会偷你的钱包，但这取决于你的穿着。

paragraphs.en: "Horizontal pockets that are really tight with tight jeans are hard; back pockets are easier," he says. Even better, he adds, "If your purse or your backpack is on your back and your zipper isn't completely zipped up."
paragraphs.zh: “与紧身牛仔裤一起穿时，水平口袋真的很紧，很难用；后口袋更容易，”他说。他补充道，更好的情况是，“如果你的手提包或背包背在背上，并且拉链没有完全拉上。”

paragraphs.en: Lifting wallets was part of his training for the new film, The Only Living Pickpocket in New York. In it, Turturro stars as Harry, a skilled pickpocket who is also the primary caretaker for his wife, who's in a catatonic state. Harry's life takes a turn when he steals the backpack of a college-age kid who turns out to be the grandson of a crime boss.
paragraphs.zh: 偷钱包是他为新电影《纽约唯一的活捡贼》进行训练的一部分。在片中，图图罗饰演哈利，一个技术娴熟的小偷，同时也是他处于昏迷状态妻子的主要照顾者。当哈利偷了一个大学生的背包时，他的生活发生了转折，而这个大学生竟然是一个犯罪老大的孙子。

paragraphs.en: To prepare for the role, Turturro practiced with Apollo Robbins, a famed sleight-of-hand artist, who coached him on the art of misdirection. "He really helped me, gave me exercises, and worked with me," Turturro says. "I [practiced picking pockets] in the production office and on the set all the time."
paragraphs.zh: 为了准备这个角色，特图罗与著名的手法艺术家阿波罗·罗宾斯一起练习，他指导特图罗掌握了转移注意力的技巧。特图罗说：“他真的帮了我，给了我练习，并与我一起训练。我经常在制片办公室和片场练习扒窃。”

paragraphs.en: Harry isn't the first morally dubious character Turturro's played during his lengthy career in Hollywood. His film credits include Five Corners, The Big Lebowski, O Brother, Where Art Thou? and Do the Right Thing. In recent years, he's been on TV in the critically acclaimed series The Night Of, The Plot Against America, and Severance.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里并不是图图罗在好莱坞漫长职业生涯中扮演的第一个道德可疑的角色。他的电影作品包括《五角街区》、《大保龄球》、《哦兄弟，你到哪儿去了？》和《做正确的事》。近年来，他在电视上出演了备受好评的系列剧《夜晚》、《反美国阴谋》和《分裂》。

paragraphs.en: Turturro says he's attracted to complex roles — and he's always willing to learn something new: "I really do try to take the elevator down into the sub-basement and mine everything I possibly can because I'm a student," he says. "I love to begin something because you never know. There's the unknown of, 'I may fail. I may not be able to do that.' And I find that exciting."
paragraphs.zh: 图图罗说他被复杂的角色所吸引——而且他总是愿意学习新事物：“我真的会尽量乘电梯下到地下室，尽可能挖掘一切，因为我是一名学生，”他说。“我喜欢开始某件事，因为你永远不知道。总有未知，比如‘我可能会失败，我可能做不到。’而我觉得这很令人兴奋。”

paragraphs.en: On being a legal guardian to his late brother who had schizophrenia
paragraphs.zh: 作为他已故患有精神分裂症的兄弟的法定监护人

paragraphs.en: I had to find different residences and then I put him in an apartment. I had to hire all the aides and then someone who was in charge of the aides so I could function and he wasn't used to being outside [the hospital]. So a lot of times he was not appreciative of that. He could be very abusive and very unpredictable, so you never knew what was going to happen. So I was always on sort of a high alert. No matter where I was in the world, I tried to protect my own family from him. And then eventually we finally got him on a medicine which he could take monthly. …
paragraphs.zh: 我不得不寻找不同的住所，然后我把他安排在一个公寓里。我不得不雇佣所有的护理人员，然后找一个负责这些护理人员的人，这样我才能正常运作，而他不习惯在[医院]之外的环境。所以很多时候他并不感激这一点。他可能非常虐待人，也非常不可预测，所以你永远不知道会发生什么。所以我总是处于一种高度警戒状态。无论我身处世界的哪个地方，我都尽力保护自己的家人不受他的伤害。最后我们终于让他服用一种每月一次的药物……

paragraphs.zh: 安迪·泰格和詹姆斯·珀塞尔正试图成为有史以来第一个完成桌面游戏《北非战役》的玩家。这个游戏如此复杂，可能需要几十年才能完成。

paragraphs.en: In the U.K., two friends have begun a challenge that many people believe is impossible. The board game Campaign for North Africa is legendary for its complexity and detail and its extreme time commitment. Andy Taeger and James Purcell are trying to become the first people ever to complete it. Hi to both of you.
paragraphs.zh: 在英国，两个朋友开始了一项许多人认为不可能完成的挑战。棋盘游戏《北非战役》以其复杂性、细节丰富和极高的时间投入而闻名。安迪·泰格和詹姆斯·珀塞尔正试图成为有史以来第一个完成它的人。向你们两位问好。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: So this board game covers a period of World War II that lasted roughly three years. Yet the game itself could take almost 10 times that, you know, many years more. What is it that makes it what you guys have described as comically complicated?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：所以这个棋盘游戏涵盖了二战时期大约三年的时间。然而，游戏本身可能需要几乎十倍的时间，你知道，也就是多年。究竟是什么让它变成了你们所描述的滑稽复杂？

paragraphs.en: PURCELL: I suppose, first and foremost, we aren't generals. So we have no experience in warfare. There is everything to keep track of in this game down to how much water each unit has to drink, how much of that water evaporates, just about every granular detail you can think of.
paragraphs.zh: 普塞尔：我想，最重要的是，我们不是将军。因此我们没有战争经验。在这个游戏中，有太多事情需要跟踪，包括每个单位需要喝多少水、有多少水会蒸发，你能想到的几乎每一个细节。

paragraphs.en: TAEGER: There's a rule Italian infantry uses more water so they could boil their pasta.
paragraphs.zh: TAEGER：意大利步兵有一个规定，就是使用更多的水，这样他们就可以煮意大利面。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: The pasta is that the Italians are going to go through drinking water faster, and they need to calculate that in?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：意大利人喝水会更快，而他们需要把这一点计算在内吗？

paragraphs.en: PURCELL: Yeah. Apparently, they have to use more to boil their pasta. I'm not sure how accurate that is, but that's part of the rules.
paragraphs.zh: 普塞尔：是的。显然，他们必须用更多的水来煮意大利面。我不确定这有多准确，但这是规则的一部分。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: All right, so the big question is - why? Why are the two of you doing this, if you know it could take years or even decades to complete?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：好吧，那么大问题是——为什么？如果你们知道这可能需要几年甚至几十年才能完成，你们为什么还要做这件事？

paragraphs.en: PURCELL: We'd love to give an answer that makes some aspect of sense, but we really don't know why we're doing this.
paragraphs.zh: 珀塞尔：我们很希望给出一个有某种意义的回答，但我们真的不知道自己为什么要这样做。

articles.title: 'Grasping at straws': Judge dismisses Trump suit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein letter
articles.dek: Saying the president was "grasping at straws," a federal judge on Saturday threw out Donald Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and media mogul Rupert Murdoch over a story…

paragraphs.en: Saying the president was "grasping at straws," a federal judge on Saturday threw out Donald Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and media mogul Rupert Murdoch over a story reporting on his ties to Jeffrey Epstein.
paragraphs.zh: 一位联邦法官在周六表示，总统是在“抓救命稻草”，并驳回了唐纳德·特朗普针对《华尔街日报》和媒体大亨鲁珀特·默多克关于报道他与杰弗里·爱泼斯坦关系的新闻提起的100亿美元诉讼。

paragraphs.en: U.S. District Judge Darrin Gayles in Miami dismissed the suit with prejudice, ruling that the president did not prove the defendants made defamatory statements with actual malice as required by law. The ruling said the lawsuit had attempted to "manufacture" flaws in the Journal's investigative reporting.
paragraphs.zh: 迈阿密的美国地方法官达林·盖尔斯（Darrin Gayles）以有偏见的方式驳回了这起诉讼，裁定总统未能证明被告按照法律要求以实际恶意发表了诽谤性言论。裁决指出，这起诉讼试图“捏造”《华尔街日报》调查报道中的缺陷。

paragraphs.en: When a case is thrown out "with prejudice," it cannot be refiled again and the dismissal is permanent and incontrovertible.
paragraphs.zh: 当案件被以“有偏见”的理由驳回时，不能再次提起诉讼，该驳回是永久且无可争辩的。

paragraphs.en: The dismissal is a blow to Trump and his administration, which have both pursued adversarial relationships with news organizations during his second term. In addition to the Journal, he is embroiled in lawsuits involving the BBC, The Associated Press and — most recently — CNN, MS NOW and Politico, which are suing him for restored access after he banished them from the White House in mid-September.
paragraphs.zh: 这次解职对特朗普及其政府是一次打击，他们在第二任期内一直与新闻机构保持对抗关系。除了《华尔街日报》，他还卷入了涉及英国广播公司、美联社以及——最近——CNN、MS NOW和Politico的诉讼，这些机构正在起诉他以恢复访问权限，此前他在九月中旬将它们驱逐出白宫。

paragraphs.en: Trump has denounced media outlets that write things to which he objects and frequently calls them "fake news" and insults their journalists.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普谴责那些写出他反对内容的媒体，并经常称它们为“假新闻”，还侮辱它们的记者。

paragraphs.en: The White House did not immediately react publicly to Saturday's dismissal or respond to an AP request for comment.
paragraphs.zh: 白宫没有立即就周六的解雇作出公开反应，也没有回应美联社的置评请求。

paragraphs.en: The lawsuit against the Journal was over a story it published last year describing a sexually suggestive letter and drawing that the paper said bore Trump's name and was included in a 2003 album compiled for Epstein's 50th birthday.
paragraphs.zh: 对该报的诉讼是关于它去年发表的一篇报道，该报道描述了一封具有性暗示的信件和一幅画，报纸称这些信件和画作署有特朗普的名字，并被收录在为爱泼斯坦50岁生日编制的2003年相册中。

paragraphs.en: The letter was reportedly collected by disgraced British socialite Ghislaine Maxwell as part of a birthday album for Epstein years before he was first arrested in 2006 and subsequently had a falling-out with Trump.
paragraphs.zh: 据报道，这封信是由声名狼藉的英国社交名流吉丝兰·麦克斯韦收集的，作为为埃普斯坦制作的生日相册的一部分，这发生在他2006年首次被逮捕之前的几年，之后他与特朗普反目成仇。

articles.title: Your writing was flagged as AI. What does that actually mean?
articles.dek: Ghostwriter Sally McGraw was hoping to land a job developing a book proposal for a prospective client. But after submitting a writing sample, she got an unexpected response: an email telling her…

paragraphs.en: Ghostwriter Sally McGraw was hoping to land a job developing a book proposal for a prospective client. But after submitting a writing sample, she got an unexpected response: an email telling her that multiple artificial intelligence detection tools had flagged her work as machine-generated.
paragraphs.zh: 代笔作家萨莉·麦格劳希望获得一份为潜在客户开发书籍提案的工作。但在提交写作样本后，她收到了一份意想不到的回复：一封电子邮件告诉她，多个人工智能检测工具已经将她的作品标记为机器生成。

paragraphs.en: "I was floored because I had not used AI to generate the text," McGraw said. "I'd written it all myself."
paragraphs.zh: 麦格劳说：“我震惊了，因为我没有用人工智能来生成这段文字，我完全是自己写的。”

paragraphs.en: Having spent more than 20 years as a professional nonfiction writer, McGraw said she was angry that her work had been dismissed as AI-written.
paragraphs.zh: 麦格劳说，作为一名拥有超过20年经验的专业非虚构作家，她对自己的作品被认为是人工智能写的而感到愤怒。

paragraphs.en: "You know where you see a cartoon character going red from their chin all the way up to the crown of their head? I felt my ears starting to burn," she said. "I thought, what is going on?"
paragraphs.zh: “你知道在卡通里你看到一个角色从下巴一直红到头顶的情景吗？我感觉我的耳朵也开始发热了，”她说。“我当时想，发生什么事了？”

paragraphs.en: McGraw said she assured the client she had written the proposal herself, but decided not to press the issue because she considered the job "minor."
paragraphs.zh: 麦格劳说她向客户保证自己亲自撰写了提案，但她决定不再坚持这个问题，因为她认为这份工作“微不足道”。

paragraphs.en: In an email to NPR, the client confirmed that she had screened McGraw's work for AI. But she said the results were not the determining factor in choosing to hire a different writer, instead citing experience and fit. McGraw says she was paid for her writing samples, but believes the detector results cost her the opportunity to write the full book proposal.
paragraphs.zh: 在给NPR的电子邮件中，这位客户确认她已经对麦格劳的作品进行了人工智能检测。但她表示，检测结果并不是选择雇用其他作者的决定性因素，而是引用了经验和契合度。麦格劳表示，她为自己的写作样本获得了报酬，但认为检测结果让她失去了撰写完整书籍提案的机会。

paragraphs.en: As editors struggle to keep up with a growing influx of AI-generated content, some are turning to detection tools to help sift through the mounting number of submissions. But these tools aren't perfect: They've been known to falsely flag human-written work as AI, which can leave writers with little idea of what triggered the result and how to prove otherwise.
paragraphs.zh: 随着编辑们努力跟上不断增长的 AI 生成内容，一些人开始使用检测工具来帮助筛选不断增加的投稿数量。但这些工具并不完美：它们已知会错误地将人工撰写的作品标记为 AI，这可能让作者对触发结果的原因几乎一无所知，也不知如何证明其作品是人工创作的。

paragraphs.en: "Everyone knows that these screeners are not 100% accurate," said McGraw.
paragraphs.zh: 麦格劳说：“每个人都知道这些筛查器并不是百分之百准确。”
